node.wording: What does exhaustive checking of all 16 assignments for one four-variable formula establish about a proposed extension, and does it prove every residual CNF has a total extension and is easy to solve?

node.boundary: One specified Boolean formula with four variables; the finite domain is exactly its 16 assignments.
node.state: The proposed extension is evaluated on each assignment to this single formula.
node.rules: Check whether the extension returns a value for every assignment and whether that value is unique.
node.grammar: Boolean assignments to four variables; no family of formulas or residual CNFs is enumerated.
node.possibilities: Exactly 2^4 = 16 input assignments for the instance.
node.realisation: An exhaustive program check reports totality and single-valuedness on that instance.
node.residual: No conclusions about other formulas or residual CNFs follow from this instance alone.
node.cost: No runtime, asymptotic, or resource-cost measurements are given.
node.grounding: Synthetic case statement; source standard on explicit scope reporting.
node.test: Finite exhaustive check of the instance only; no universal proof or complexity analysis.

node.wording: For this one four-variable formula, the proposed extension is total and single-valued over all 16 assignments, conditional on the checker and its specification being correct.
node.scope: Only the specified instance and its complete 16-assignment domain.
node.author: research assistant

node.wording: The finite check does not prove that every residual CNF has a total extension or that the general problem is easy to solve.
node.scope: Universal existence/totality and general computational difficulty across residual CNFs.
node.author: research assistant

node.description: Synthetic case says all 16 assignments for one four-variable formula were checked; the proposed extension was total and single-valued on that instance.
node.role: Direct finite-instance evidence for the scoped result.

node.description: The case explicitly states that no other formulas and no runtime/cost measures were checked.
node.role: Limitation: no cross-instance or tractability evidence.

node.title: Doing Science Research on the OCELOT Substrate

node.wording: An extension may fail to be total or single-valued on another formula, and solving may be costly even if a total extension exists; this case did not test either possibility.
node.scope: Other residual CNFs and computational cost, outside the enumerated instance.

edge.rationale: Exhaustive checking covers the whole finite input domain of the stated instance.
The record says explicitly that no other formulas or cost measures were checked.
This is a counterpossibility to universal extrapolation, not a demonstrated counterexample.
§7.1 requires explicit statements of what a result establishes and does not establish.
